candidate_relations.reason: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma is a compatible CD30-positive ALK-negative subtype within peripheral T-cell lymphoma but is more specific than the requested PTCL-NHL object.
Subacute hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis captures extreme ferritin and cytopenias as a lymphoma-associated manifestation, not peripheral T-cell NHL.
Hematological malignancy is the parent of marrow-replacing lymphoma and omits peripheral T-cell NHL.
Infection is a febrile differential; cultures were sterile and marrow showed high-grade T-cell tumor.
HLH physiology (cytopenias, extreme ferritin) is a related inflammatory manifestation of T-cell lymphoma, not the lymphoma itself.
Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis is a different autoinflammatory disease in a 32-year-old.
T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma is the parent lineage and omits the required peripheral (mature) qualifier.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is an incompatible B-cell lineage versus CD3/cytotoxic T-cell markers.
T-cell lymphoma is a parent of peripheral T-cell NHL and omits the peripheral/NHL specification.
Hematophagic histiocytosis is an HLH-type manifestation, not peripheral T-cell NHL.
Peripheral T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma matches the reference and the CD2/CD3/CD30 cytotoxic, ALK-negative marrow lymphoma.
NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type, is an incompatible extranodal NK/T entity; no nasal disease is described.
Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma is a related cytotoxic lymphoma with incompatible NK/T rather than peripheral T-cell NHL classification.
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is an incompatible CD30-positive lymphoma versus T-cell NHL (cytoplasmic CD3, cytotoxic markers, ALK-negative).
Peripheral T-cell lymphoma is an alias of peripheral T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Castleman disease is a different lymphoproliferative disorder.
Myelodysplastic syndrome is a different marrow failure neoplasm, not high-grade T-cell lymphoma.
Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma is a related PTCL subtype without typical AITL features here, so it conflicts as a named subtype versus the requested peripheral T-cell NHL object.
ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma conflicts with ALK-1 negativity.
Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis is a different self-limited lymphadenitis, not marrow-replacing T-cell lymphoma.

case_quality_flags: Marrow IHC is CD30-positive cytotoxic T-cell (ALK-negative), so ALK-negative ALCL is a plausible subtype within peripheral T-cell lymphoma.
